inclusion_rule: Include speech-decoding studies (recognition, classification or synthesis of overt, whispered, silent or imagined speech) that record scalp or around-ear EEG together with surface EMG of the speech muscles and report decoding from EEG, EMG or their combination. Boundary: studies that record EMG only to remove or measure artifacts in EEG count as pattern matches but are recorded as artifact-control designs, not fusion; non-speech EEG-EMG fusion (limb movement), reviews and datasets without decoding are excluded; versions of one study count once.

usual_approach.note: full-text pattern counts over the 30 unique studies whose ledger names both scalp_eeg and surface_emg; eeg_emg_fusion 10

read_fulltext.quote: This is the first attempt to convert silent signals into audio by fus- ing EEG and sEMG signals.
an average objec- tive character error rate (CER) of 7.22% among eight speakers is obtained.

However, EEG-based speech decoding remains controversial especially for overt speech, due to difficulties in separating speech-related neural activities from myoelectric potential artifacts generated during articulation.
For EEG data, a band-pass filter between 0.5–200 Hz was applied, while for EMG data, a high-pass filter with a cutoff of 2 Hz was used.

state_of_the_art.metric: ASR CER of EEG+sEMG silent-speech synthesis, 8 speakers, held-out repeats of training sentences (EEG only 38.85%, sEMG only 10.52%)
